Contractor personnel will work with Air National Guard (ANG) fighter aircrew to optimize physical performance targeting neck and back pain prevention while monitoring, analyzing, and resolving physical readiness concerns. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as Government Furnished, to perform Massage Therapy and Preventive Physical Therapy Services, as defined in this PWS. 1.1.1 Objectives: The purpose of the OHWS program is to reduce the frequency and severity of neck and back pain injuries, reduce duty time lost, improve quality of life, enhance readiness, and support fighter aircrew retention. The contract services must, at a minimum, deliver the services identified in Section 4.0 of this PWS and use available facilities so personnel will have convenient access to the Contract specialists. The Contractor goal is to reduce injury rates and to increase the rate of fighter aircrew fully mission capable status. 1.2 Background: In 2019 Air Combat Command (ACC) published a new requirement, which supports Regular Air Force (RegAF) Combat Air Forces (CAF) fighter squadrons at locations in Air Combat Command (ACC), Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), and United States Air Forces Europe (USAFE). hat follows or exceeds manufacturer’s recommended procedures or the applicable sections of the Inter-Range Instrumentation Group (IRIG) Standards. The contractor shall perform continuous system assessments necessary to provide effective maintenance and sustainment reporting at various reviews defined in Sections 3 and 4. The WFF currently utilizes the United States Air Force Instrumentation Radar Support Program (IRSP), which can be referenced at https://irsp.com/ , to perform varying Depot Level Maintenance (DLM) activities for Wallops Range radars and provide critical spares for radar systems. The contractor shall define how they propose to perform DLM activities for the range instrumentation systems along with the estimated costs per year to implement the approach and justification of the choice made. If the contractor chooses to utilize the IRSP for systems other than radars (radars are required to utilize the IRSP for DLM activities), these estimated costs and justifications for approach shall also be defined. The contractor shall provide controlled access to

Range Surveillance Operations. The S3 shall interface with video data communication interfaces for distribution of displays throughout the control center. The contractor shall assume system administration of the APS-143 ground station computers located in the RCC. Contractor personnel shall have operational responsibility of the Wallops SureTrak in Government (STING) system located in the RCC. Operations shall include pre-mission setup. Pre-mission setup shall include entering launch trajectory and impact points into the system, which will be used to perform impact probability calculations. The contractor shall enter reference locations, enable mission archiving, and create and upload hazard patterns for display. Historical photograph negatives shall be scanned and entered into the digital image database throughout the contract and performed on a non-interference basis with other Wallops Range support requirements. AOI 01: EF Technology Sprints - Activated Digital Thread for Battlefield Responsiveness AFRL is seeking innovative solutions to operationalize digital architecture capable of responding to battlefield dynamics in near real-time. The objective is to close the loop between battlefield data and the manufacturing floor, creating an adaptive manufacturing ecosystem that expedites the re-configuration of weapon systems to enhance warfighter lethality. Solutions are sought to drastically reduce design-to-field cycle times by addressing one or more of the following technical challenges: (1) Model-Based Quality Assurance & Digital Certification. Goal: Transition from physical-test-dependent to analysis-led certification. To realize surge manufacturing, the bottleneck of physical requalification for every design change must be eliminated. Solutions are sought that leverage Certification by Analysis (CbA) and probabilistic simulation to validate manufacturing variability and design changes. Approaches should address how seamless data interchange can support certification allowing for rapid acceptance of re-configured components without extensive physical testing campaigns. (2) Modular Integration & Factorial Manufacturing. Goal: Enable "Plug-and-Play"
